note:
Reviewed CDB90 match 224, pinned revision e0b35ec4d798cec3bb4e6970c0f6bb7aa69e2f4c. CDB90 (CAA Database of Battles, Version 1990), tidy data maintained by Jeffrey B. Arnold. Original US Army Concepts Analysis Agency data; revised data licensed ODC-BY. Original force designations and strength interpretations are retained with each quantity. Each side is one aggregate force, including any coalition; its total is not allocated among members. Personnel casualties are not deaths. Source estimates and adjudged error margins are not statistical confidence intervals. Equipment and tactical movements are not established by this dataset. Match review: GER 1ST & 2ND ARMIES stays a combined local formation; do not invent a post-1871 German Empire identity.

The Archives d’Alsace account identifies the French 94th line regiment in Canrobert’s 6th Corps at Saint-Privat on 18 August, within Bazaine’s imperial Army of the Rhine. The retained CDB label FR ARMY OF LORRAINE is not renamed. The kepi, blue-grey campaign capote, garance trousers and Chassepot M1866 with sabre bayonet are a documented 1870 line-infantry analogy. Clothing, regiment, supply and branch varied; this is not a claim that every soldier of the mixed army wore or carried these items. Zouaves, tirailleurs, guards, mobiles, cavalry and artillery are not converted into line infantry. No component proportion, new participant, strength, loss or death is inferred. The Draner print used for visual corroboration was published in 1871; it is not dated to the battle and does not broaden the profile’s eligibility.

The institutional Deutsche Biographie entry for Decken identifies his transfer into the Prussian army, command of its 6th Infantry Brigade in July 1870 and participation at Gravelotte. This establishes a Prussian line-infantry component within the retained GER 1ST & 2ND ARMIES aggregate; it does not make every allied formation Prussian. The leather spiked helmet, blue tunic, grey trousers and Dreyse M1862 form a representative 1870 Prussian line-infantry analogy. Helmet patterns, regimental details, clothing and equipment varied. The Auxonne helmet is a surviving November 1870 trophy, not an object proven to have been at this battle; the Carnavalet print shows several forms of dress. No fixed bayonet or precise regimental badge is reconstructed. The equipment identity Q27306 is a gate for this reviewed component only. Existing participant IDs, names, aggregate membership, all strengths, losses and deaths remain unchanged; no infantry share is inferred. Cavalry, artillery, guards, riflemen and allied states are not recategorized as this line-infantry component.
